sources.agency: Colorado Secretary of State, Elections Division
sources.title: Voter registration statistics, sheet 'Voter Counts by Precinct' (the newest monthly workbook)
sources.about: Every 2026 precinct's ten-digit number (congressional, Senate and House district, county, number in the county); only those two cells are read. Used as a check (listed_2026).

notes.lines: Every precinct, county, congressional and legislative line is a 2020 census block's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre). A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.precincts: Colorado publishes no statewide map of its precincts as they stand in 2026 that can be read here. Each shape is a voting district as the county reported it to the Census Bureau for the 2020 census, cut wherever a congressional or legislative district of the 2021 plans, a city or town limit or an RTD director district crosses it. The counties re-precincted after 2021, so the county clerk is the authority on a voter's precinct. listed_2026 marks a piece whose 2020 number is a 2026 precinct number of its county in the Secretary of State's list, whose own digits give the piece's congressional, Senate and House district (code_2026_said gives that ten-digit number). What a ballot depends on (county, congressional, Senate and House district, judicial district, city or town, RTD director district, school district) does not depend on the precinct.
notes.places: Colorado's incorporated cities and towns (Denver and Broomfield are each a city and county) have no townships around them. A precinct piece lies wholly inside one city or town (mcd) or outside every one: a piece in unincorporated country names no place. A block is given to the city or town its own inside point lies in, by the limits of January 1, 2025, so a recent annexation that cuts a block is drawn to the nearest block line.
notes.commissioners: No statewide file has the lines of county commissioner districts; each county keeps its own (commissioners are elected by the whole county with a residence district, or by district in a few home rule counties).
notes.legislative: Each of the 65 House districts and 35 Senate districts elects one member. Which district a block is in is the Census Bureau's 2024 equivalency file's word for the 2021 plans, so a precinct piece's districts are exact.
notes.boards: The State Board of Education and the University of Colorado's Board of Regents each have one seat elected by each congressional district (and members elected statewide); sboe and regent name the seat a precinct votes for.
notes.rtd: The Regional Transportation District's fifteen directors are elected by director district. rtd names the district a piece lies in; a piece outside the RTD has none. RTD is the authority on its districts.
notes.school: School district lines are the Census Bureau's 2025 file. Which districts a precinct piece lies in is analysis, not an official list: a district counts when its piece of the precinct is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each district's share of the piece's area (land and water, not voters). School boards are elected in odd-numbered years.
notes.judicial: The 23 judicial districts are whole counties (C.R.S. 13-5-102 to 13-5-123.1); district court judges stand for retention in them, and county court judges in their county.
notes.wards: No statewide file has the lines of city council districts or wards: a council district's race is placed on its city, and the city clerk says which district an address is in.
notes.authority: For which precinct an address is in, the county clerk and recorder is the authority; for where to vote, GoVoteColorado and the county clerk.
notes.precinct_ids: A precinct's id is its county's five digits, a full stop and the Census Bureau's 2020 voting district code (08001.001230); a voting district cut by a district line, a city limit or an RTD line has a second full stop and the piece's number.

format.files: Every file is TopoJSON on one grid (transform above): arcs are delta-encoded lines; a shape's arcs name the lines of its rings, a negative number n meaning line ~n backwards; outer rings run counter-clockwise, holes clockwise.
format.county_files: precincts/<county>.json, object 'precincts': one shape per precinct piece. arcMask[i] has bit k set when line i is an outline of arc_kinds[k]; arcSides[2i] and arcSides[2i+1] are the precincts on the right and left of line i (-1: a precinct in another county's file; -2: outside Colorado); names gives the names of the places the file's precincts lie in.
format.boxes: boxes[county] holds four whole numbers a precinct, in the file's order: west, south, east, north in steps of box_step degrees from the transform's translate, rounded outwards. A point is tried against every precinct whose box (widened by half a step) holds it.

precinct_properties.name: the precinct's name: the 2020 voting district's as the Census Bureau's file gives it (the county and the precinct's number), and the piece's number where a line cuts it
precinct_properties.precinct: the county's five digits and the Bureau's 2020 voting district code
precinct_properties.as_of: the year of the precinct's lines (2020)
precinct_properties.listed_2026: true where the Secretary of State's 2026 list has a precinct of the county with the same number whose own digits give the piece's congressional, Senate and House district
precinct_properties.code_2026_said: with listed_2026: that 2026 precinct's ten-digit number
precinct_properties.mcd: the city or town the piece lies in (absent in unincorporated country)
precinct_properties.sboe: State Board of Education district (CO-CD1 Congressional District 1, CO-CD2 Congressional District 2, CO-CD3 Congressional District 3, CO-CD4 Congressional District 4, CO-CD5 Congressional District 5, CO-CD6 Congressional District 6, CO-CD7 Congressional District 7, CO-CD8 Congressional District 8): the congressional district of the same number
precinct_properties.regent: Regent of the University of Colorado district (CO-CD1 Congressional District 1, CO-CD2 Congressional District 2, CO-CD3 Congressional District 3, CO-CD4 Congressional District 4, CO-CD5 Congressional District 5, CO-CD6 Congressional District 6, CO-CD7 Congressional District 7, CO-CD8 Congressional District 8): the congressional district of the same number
precinct_properties.rtd: Regional Transportation District director district (absent outside the RTD; CO-X-RTD-A A, CO-X-RTD-B B, CO-X-RTD-C C, CO-X-RTD-D D, CO-X-RTD-E E, CO-X-RTD-F F, CO-X-RTD-G G, CO-X-RTD-H H, CO-X-RTD-I I, CO-X-RTD-J J, CO-X-RTD-K K, CO-X-RTD-L L, CO-X-RTD-M M, CO-X-RTD-N N, CO-X-RTD-O O)
precinct_properties.school: list: the school districts the piece lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.school_pct: list, when the piece is in more than one: each district's share of its area, in percent
precinct_properties.school_out: percent of the piece's area that lies in no school district (given from 3 percent up)
precinct_properties.school_edge: list: neighbouring districts that only brush the piece along a line (try them too when placing a point)
precinct_properties.c: a point inside the piece's largest part, for a label: [longitude, latitude]

ids.every layer: a shape's properties j and d are the jurisdiction id and the district its races carry on the ballot pages
ids.mcd: CO-M- and the Census Bureau's place code (CO-M-20000); properties.t says city or town
ids.cd: the district (1); properties.j is CO-CD1, the jurisdiction of the State Board of Education's and the regents' seats; properties.race is the race for Congress
ids.judicial: CO-JD and the district's number (CO-JD2); d is the number
ids.school: CO-S- and the Census Bureau's five-digit district code (CO-S-03360); properties.nces is the federal district code
ids.rtd: a precinct property only: CO-X-RTD- and the director district's letter (CO-X-RTD-B)
ids.sboe and regent: precinct properties only: CO-CD and the congressional district's number
